- **FLARE is the headline 2024-2026 milestone**: Ji is the named Principal Investigator of the new FLARE user facility at PPPL, inaugurated on June 12, 2025 with DOE Office of Science / Fusion Energy Sciences backing. -> The strongest single piece of public funding-adjacent evidence in the window.

- **NSF active-award search returned nothing** under Ji as PI at Princeton; PPPL researchers are typically funded via DOE-SC/FES through the lab contract, not as standalone NSF PIs. -> No NSF award line to record; absence is consistent with funding model.

- **LinkedIn surface is limited**: Only Ji's personal profile (570+ followers) is publicly visible; no post advertising an open position was located. -> Use as discovery evidence only, not as primary confirmation.

content.recent_and_active_funding_announced_on_o:
### FLARE user facility (DOE/SC, Fusion Energy Sciences)

- **What it is**: Facility for Laboratory Reconnection Experiments. A first-of-a-kind pulsed-power device ~12 ft long, 9 ft in diameter, >10 tons, capable of discharging more than 6 MJ per shot - producing plasma conditions that simulate astrophysical magnetic reconnection at laboratory scale.
- **Funder**: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Science, Fusion Energy Sciences (FES). Confirmed by the presence of DOE Office of Science (Christian Newton, chief of staff) and DOE FES (Jean Paul Allain, associate director) at the inauguration.
- **Award/announcement date**: Ribbon-cutting June 12, 2025; Princeton/PPPL news release June 13, 2025.
- **Ji role**: Named Principal Investigator of FLARE on the official press release.
- **Status**: Active as of June 2025; described as a new user facility open to the scientific community.
- **Public amount and currency**: **Not publicly disclosed** in the available press release. No dollar figure could be verified in open sources. -> Do not invent or estimate a budget.
- **What the funded work does**: Provides a laboratory platform to study magnetic reconnection under controlled conditions relevant to solar flares, magnetospheric physics, and disruptions in tokamak fusion plasmas.
- **Source URLs**:
  - https://www.princeton.edu/news/2025/06/13/unprecedented-new-device-pppl-will-help-unravel-mysteries-universe
  - https://www.pppl.gov/FLARE
  - https://www.pppl.gov/news (FLARE inauguration entry)

> Caveat: DOE national-laboratory user facilities are typically funded through the managing contractor's prime award (Princeton University for PPPL) plus specific line-item construction / Major Item of Equipment (MIE) funding from DOE/SC. The public press materials confirm FES sponsorship but do not publish a separate dollar amount attributable to Ji as PI.

### 2025 John Dawson Award for Excellence in Plasma Physics Research (APS)

- **What it is**: Competitive award recognizing "outstanding achievements in plasma physics research" from the APS Division of Plasma Physics.
- **Funder / issuer**: American Physical Society, Division of Plasma Physics.
- **Announcement date**: November 2025 (award ceremony at APS DPP meeting; ceremony video on Ji's homepage dated November 19, 2025).
- **Recipients**: Hantao Ji, Jeremy Goodman, Fatima Ebrahimi, Yin Wang, Erik Gilson (per the EurekAlert release).
- **Ji role**: Co-recipient (the citation credits Ji as principal investigator of the laboratory MRI program at PPPL).
- **Status**: Conferred.
- **Public amount**: APS does not publish a cash prize amount for the Dawson Award in the materials reviewed.
- **What it recognizes**: "For the first laboratory realization and theoretical investigations of both the hydrodynamic stability and the magneto-rotational instability in axisymmetric and non-axisymmetric forms that were proposed to operate in accretion plasmas to form planets, stars, and supermassive black holes."
- **Source URLs**:
  - https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1100143
  - https://w3.pppl.gov/~hji/ (Ji homepage news section)
  - https://www.pppl.gov/news/2025/laboratory-breakthrough-recreating-star-formation-mechanism-wins-prestigious-john-dawson

> This is included for completeness because the lead asks to distinguish a competitive grant from a prize. The Dawson Award is a competitive *recognition*, not a research grant; it does not carry research funding.

### NSF Award Search (public API)

- **Query executed**: NSF Award Search advanced search, PI last name = Ji, PI first name = Hantao, organization includes Princeton, ActiveAwards = true.
- **Result**: **0 active awards returned** for Hantao Ji at Princeton as PI in the NSF database (as accessed via the public NSF search interface).
- **Interpretation**: Consistent with PPPL's funding model, where plasma-physics PIs are primarily supported through DOE-SC/FES via the Princeton/PPPL management contract rather than as standalone NSF PIs.
- **Source URL**: https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/advancedSearch.jsp (queried; no results)

### Other PPPL / DOE items

- No additional publicly itemized competitive grant award (with a public dollar value and award number) attributable to Hantao Ji as PI in 2024-2026 could be retrieved in this research session. The PPPL press archive mentions ongoing MRI and reconnection research outputs (papers, conference talks) but not new grant line items.
- **Source URL attempted**: https://www.pppl.gov/news (FLARE and Dawson entries cited above)
